newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals prices mixed, gold off.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals prices mixed, gold off.

text.p: Precious metals prices mostly turned easier on Monday afternoon as buying interest from the U.S. investments funds waned, dealers said.
Short covering by the funds was the driving force behind the gold market's rise from under $320.00 per ounce last week, encouraged by gold finding a floor about the $318.50-$319.50 level.
On Monday gold fixed at $326.20 down from $328.05 at the morning fixing and compared with $323.20 on Friday afternoon.
At the fixing the Comex August contract was down about $2.20 at $327.40.

The fixes since Friday have been the first time gold has achieved these levels since July 3 when the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves and sent the price on its way to its lowest levels in 12 years.
The market became severely oversold in the descent leading some dealers to expect an upward reaction.
The investment funds on Comex had around 90,000 lots of short positions at the peak of the bear rush.
On Friday latest Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitment of Traders' data showed that figure had come into 74,588 lots on July 15 and was expected to show further declines.
However some market analysts were doubtful that the recent short covering represented a significant shift in fund manager thinking.
"The idea last month that going short was the correct decision hasn't suddenly become wrong," one market analyst said.

A decline in U.S. stock market levels may have helped gold on Friday, dealers said, and one analyst noted a "textbook" boost for gold when gold mining shares rose on Friday against the general stock market trend.
Meanwhile the other precious metals were mixed with silver easier and platinum and palladium mostly holding earlier firmer levels.
Silver was indicated at $4.28/$4.30 down a cent from Friday's close and a couple of cents off Friday's close.
Last Thursday silver fixed at 422.35 cents, its lowest level since November 3, 1993.
Platinum was close to its opening level at $413.00/$416.00 up $7.00 and palladium was $5.00 ahead at $188.50/$191.50
